concept.name: Point-and-figure count
concept.definition: Wyckoff's method of projecting price targets by counting the horizontal width of a trading range on a point-and-figure chart, embodying the law of cause and effect. The count measures the 'cause' built in the range and converts it into a projected 'effect' — a target zone rather than an exact destination.
concept.intuition: Measure how wide the base is, and that width tells you roughly how far the breakout should travel.
concept.mechanics: On a P&F chart of the range, the analyst selects a count line (typically at the LPS level after an SOS), counts columns from right to left phase by phase, multiplies the column tally by the box size and reversal criterion, and adds the product to the count line (maximum objective), the range low (minimum objective), and their midpoint. Stepping-stone consolidations later in the trend can produce confirming counts with smaller box sizes.
concept.formula: Target zone = anchor level +/- (n x B x R), where n = number of columns at the count line, B = box size (e.g. 0.5-1 point for low-priced stocks, ~100 for the DJIA), R = reversal criterion (typically 3); anchors are the count line, the trading-range low, and their midpoint (+ for markup targets, - for markdown targets).
concept.failure_modes: Results are highly sensitive to box size, count-line placement, and phase segmentation, all of which are discretionary; Wyckoff himself cautioned that some counts fall short and others are exceeded, so targets must be confirmed by bar-chart price and volume action.
concept.misconceptions: P&F targets are not precise reversal points; the count guide explicitly frames them as places to 'stop, look and listen', and P&F 'phases' used for counting are not the same as Phases A-E of range analysis.
concept.example: On a 100-point-box, 3-box-reversal chart of a DJIA consolidation, a 34-column count projects 34 x 100 x 3 = 10,200 points of effect; added to the range low and count line, this yields a minimum-to-maximum target band for the ensuing rally.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
